name: Deng Xiaoping
summary: Chinese Communist revolutionary and paramount leader who steered China toward market-oriented reform and opening to the world while holding to one-party Communist rule. He argued that socialism is judged by whether it develops the productive forces, allowed some people and regions to get rich first and backed foreign investment, yet insisted on public ownership, the Four Cardinal Principles and Party leadership. He rejected Western-style multiparty democracy and separated powers, ordered the 1989 crackdown on Tiananmen, and devised 'one country, two systems' for Hong Kong and Taiwan.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said a totally planned economy hampers the productive forces and that planning and the market are both just means (1985, 1987, 1992), but insisted public ownership stay predominant and the state keep control, so he did not call free markets superior.

public-ownership.rationale: Repeatedly insisted that socialist public ownership must remain predominant while allowing a private and foreign sector alongside it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Called drug abuse an evil to be stamped out by resolute measures and praised the Party for eliminating opium after 1949.

strong-leader.rationale: Criticised over-concentration of power in individuals and the personality cult, yet insisted the central leadership must have authority to carry out reform.

state-harmful.rationale: Built his programme around strengthening the socialist state and the dictatorship of the people's democracy.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Called prostitution one of the evils to stamp out and urged cracking down on the worst brothel proprietors.

decide-locally.rationale: In 1986 wanted central powers transferred to local authorities, but in 1988 insisted the central leadership must have authority over local governments.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said serious offenders should be reformed through labour or severely punished and that hesitation and light sentences had been a mistake; stressed stern punishment more than rehabilitation.

gradual-change.rationale: Said democracy can develop only gradually and political reform must be cautious, but also called reform a revolution and urged boldness and experiment.

free-trade.rationale: Pressed for opening to the outside, export orientation and foreign trade, but in 1974 attacked unequal exchange between rich and poor countries.

nation-first.rationale: Said first priority should always be given to national sovereignty and security and that China will not yield to outside pressure, while also seeking peaceful cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rejected foreign pressure over human rights as interference in China's internal affairs and criticised hegemonism, though he did not address armed intervention as such.

limit-growth.rationale: Said development is the absolute principle and that slow growth equals stagnation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said in 1990 'we should build more nuclear power stations'.

revolution-justified.rationale: Led armed revolution as a Party and army commander and wrote that revolution means emancipating the productive forces.

experts-over-public.rationale: Urged respect for knowledge and trained personnel, and promotion of professionally competent cadres, while keeping policy within Party leadership.

central-planning.rationale: Said experience showed a totally planned economy held back the productive forces and that planning must no longer be called the primary feature of socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Defended markets inside a socialist system with predominant public ownership, but also allowed private and foreign-owned firms, so the condition in the statement is only partly his.

one-party-rule.rationale: Insisted on the leadership of the Communist Party and the Four Cardinal Principles, with other parties only cooperating under CCP leadership.

democracy-best.rationale: Said democracy must be socialist democracy, not bourgeois democracy; that China must not liberalise along Western lines; and that multiparty elections would bring chaos.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred: insisted on reunifying Taiwan and keeping minority regions such as Tibet within China under regional autonomy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Defended revolutionary armed struggle and the use of troops to put down the 1989 protests.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said egalitarianism will not work and that some areas and people should get rich first, while aiming at common prosperity and avoiding polarization.

limit-population.rationale: Said in 1979 that the country must greatly increase its family-planning efforts; Wikipedia credits him with the one-child policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Made industrial and scientific modernisation his central goal.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Called science and technology a primary productive force and urged that the higher and newer the technology, the better.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Judged socialism by whether it raises productive forces and living standards, cited the 'black cat' proverb and told people to stop arguing and experiment, but treated the Four Cardinal Principles as fixed.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: his programme was rapid industrial and scientific modernisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Described socialism as the first stage of communism in which 'to each according to his needs' will apply once productive forces are highly developed; in the near term he held to distribution by work.

production-for-use.rationale: Said socialist production is meant to meet the material and cultural needs of the people rather than to exploit them.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said 'we must uphold the dictatorship of the proletariat' and in 1992 called it the defence of the socialist system, in the form of the people's democratic dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Backed the household output-quota and contract responsibility system and the end of the people's communes, while still describing collective ownership as a long-term goal.

total-state.rationale: Said the Party must not substitute for all other organisations and monopolise everything, and called for separating Party and government functions and letting the Party handle only major issues.

national-rebirth.rationale: Said modernisation is needed to revitalise the Chinese nation and win its rightful position in the world.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said China would never seek hegemony and made opposition to hegemonism the foundation of its foreign policy.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supported the independence and sovereignty of developing countries against superpower control, but denied it to Taiwan and Tibet.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged unity and cooperation among Third World countries against the hegemonism of the superpowers.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said a newly risen class must use dictatorship to consolidate its power and described the state as the people's democratic dictatorship: democracy within the people, dictatorship over the enemy.

national-mission.rationale: Said China should not demand that other countries adopt its model of revolution or order others about.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Criticised bureaucracy, privileges and corruption among Party cadres, but defended the leadership's legitimacy and blamed outside forces for the 1989 unrest.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: built and defended a state-led socialist economy with predominant public ownership and Party leadership.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: argued that socialism could be built and consolidated in China on its own road over generations.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stressed in 1992 that the socialist system must be defended by dictatorship and warned about hostile foreign pressure for peaceful evolution.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Described those who sought to overthrow the Communist Party and the socialist system as counter-revolutionary rebels and ordered action against them.

separated-powers.rationale: Said China must not copy the West's separation of the three powers and warned too much emphasis on checks and balances would cause problems, while the Party's quick decision-making is an advantage.

vanguard-party.rationale: Argued that without the leadership of a Communist Party, socialist revolution, the dictatorship of the proletariat and socialist construction would all be impossible.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Backed martial law and military force in June 1989 against what he called a counter-revolutionary rebellion, and said anything violating the law must be suppressed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Held that the Party must lead the ideological front including the press, literature and art, and in 1950 that the Party must lead newspapers; called for laws regulating press, assembly and demonstration.

party-commands-army.rationale: Said the army belongs to the Party, the people and socialism and must remain loyal to the Party; he chaired the Party's Military Commission.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Called democratic centralism the Party's fundamental organisational principle and stressed discipline, with lower bodies bound by higher decisions.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Wanted writers to foster fine morals and a socialist civilisation, supported criticism of works seen as bourgeois-liberal and condemned pornography, but in 1979 urged the unhampered development of different forms and styles in literature and art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Personally drove the abolition of life tenure in leading posts and set up retirement and advisory commissions in its place.

people-in-arms.rationale: Pursued a modern, regularised, streamlined professional army rather than reliance on the armed masses.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Made reunification of the mainland and Taiwan a central aim of his policy.

death-penalty.rationale: In his 1983 anti-crime campaign said a number of criminals should be executed according to law and that light sentences encouraged crime.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Condemned pornographic material coming into China, called for measures against it, and in 1992 demanded resolute measures to stamp out such evils.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In 1974 said loans to developing countries should allow delayed repayment or even reduction and cancellation of debts where necessary.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Said stability is the overriding need, political liberalization must not be allowed, and that less important things must be subordinated to the major task of building the country.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Told the UN that loans to developing countries should be interest-free or low-interest with delayed repayment, and later complained that the richer countries are the less generous in North-South relations.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Honoured the scientists who built China's atomic and hydrogen bombs and satellites and urged more high technology.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Said that on sovereignty over Hong Kong China had no room for manoeuvre and that no leader could justify failing to recover it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Said Taiwan's reunification would be sought peacefully but that non-peaceful means were never ruled out, and that otherwise it must be solved by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Designed 'one country, two systems': Hong Kong and Taiwan keep their capitalist system and way of life for 50 years inside China.

leader-cult.rationale: In 1956 said the Party abhors the deification of an individual, and in 1980 criticised the personality cult, including its continuation after the Gang of Four's fall.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: In 1979 said there is no bourgeoisie within the Party and none will re-emerge once exploiting classes are eliminated, rejecting the Gang of Four line; but in 1992 warned that any problem would come from inside the Party and that bourgeois liberalization must be fought.

land-redistribution.rationale: As a Party leader in 1948 pressed land reform against landlords as essential and carried it out in the Southwest.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Held that the relations of production and the superstructure must be reformed where they do not match the growth of the productive forces, and that Marxism puts developing the productive forces first.

moral-incentives.rationale: In 1978 said moral encouragement comes first and material incentives second but cannot be dispensed with; in the 1980s reform he relied heavily on material rewards (letting some get rich first).

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Called the idea that Chinese cannot run Hong Kong a leftover of the old colonial mentality and condemned colonialism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said young people must be educated in China's history and the Four Cardinal Principles and called for greater attention to the ideological education of the young.

delink-world-market.rationale: Made opening to the outside world, foreign investment and export orientation central to his programme and said China must not close its doors.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Told the UN that the superpowers and developed countries profit by pushing down raw-material prices and pushing up the prices of their own exports, plundering developing countries.

party-own-road.rationale: Said each party and people must find its own road, that China would not impose its model, and that no party should act as a patriarchal party.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In 1974 defined self-reliance as relying mainly on one's own people and resources, but from 1979 he sought foreign funds, loans and joint ventures (while saying not to borrow more than can be repaid).

return-lost-territory.rationale: Insisted China would recover Hong Kong in 1997, including Hong Kong Island and Kowloon ceded after the Opium War, and said sovereignty was non-negotiable.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Said the army and government should safeguard the socialist system and reform policies, and relied on the army in 1989.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Supported household contract farming on collectively owned land, which keeps land ownership with the collective while individuals hold use rights.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Condemned Soviet hegemonism, great-power chauvinism and invasion or subversion of other countries, naming Afghanistan among the 1980s troubles.

non-intervention.rationale: Repeatedly invoked non-interference in internal affairs as one of the Five Principles; Wikipedia notes his 1979 invasion of Vietnam, and he criticised Vietnam's presence in Kampuchea while rejecting Soviet interference.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposed hegemonism and any power telling others what to do.

defeat-communism.rationale: Was a lifelong Communist who held that only socialism and Marxism could develop China.

majority-settlement.rationale: Defended the presence of Han settlers in Tibet and Inner Mongolia as helpful to development, though he did not call for encouraging settlement as such.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said the 1989 movement aimed to overthrow the Party and must be put down, that China tolerates no disturbances, and that exponents of bourgeois liberalization who violate the law must be dealt with severely.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonialism and imperialist plunder of developing countries.

rich-first.rationale: Said some people and areas should be allowed to get rich before others and that 'to get rich is no sin'; later said the richer areas should help the poorer ones.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Opposed the hegemonism of both superpowers, said China does not treat social systems as the criterion in relations with the US or USSR, and Wikipedia describes him seeking an independent position between them; China did, however, cooperate with the US against the USSR.

term-limits.rationale: Pushed the abolition of life tenure in leading posts and a retirement system, and Wikipedia credits him with the term limits in the 1982 constitution; he did not speak of limits on numbers of terms for elected politicians in general.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Championed distribution 'to each according to his work' as a socialist principle, though he accepted profit income from private and foreign firms in the mixed economy.

independent-unions.rationale: Described trade unions as organisations through which the Party educates and mobilises workers, under the Party's leadership.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Held that socialist democracy and the people's democratic dictatorship, led by the Party, are the workers' state; did not address independent working-class power.

second-chamber.rationale: Listed a bicameral legislature among the features of Western systems China should not copy wholesale.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said non-peaceful means for Taiwan were never ruled out and, per Wikipedia, sought US approval for China's 1979 invasion of Vietnam; elsewhere stressed peace and opposition to aggression.

arms-reduction.rationale: Said China stood for arms reduction, above all by the superpowers, though he doubted disarmament talks would achieve much.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for a new international economic order and told the UN that the unequal terms of trade between raw-material producers and developed countries must be changed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Praised the development of China's atomic and hydrogen bombs in 1992 and called for arms reduction chiefly by the superpowers.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rejected multiparty elections and judged a political system by stability, unity and productive forces rather than by competitive elections; called the Chinese system better than Western-style democracy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Said no one can shake socialist China and that the socialist system must be defended against peaceful evolution toward capitalism, while himself reducing the role of planning.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: In 1950 applied the Common Programme's regional national autonomy for minority areas in the Southwest and defended the policy in 1987.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Defended Han settlement in Tibet, saying there is no harm in Han people going there to help development.

national-resource-control.rationale: In his 1974 UN speech said developing countries must keep their natural resources in their own hands and shake off foreign capital's control.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said that in the so-called multipolar world China too will be a pole, while holding it should not lead the Third World.

notes: Answers rest on his own speeches in Selected Works (marxists.org). Views changed from Maoist-era campaigns (he played a leading role in the 1957 Anti-Rightist Campaign) to the post-1978 reform line; the most recent clear position was used. Party resolutions were not used.
